sections.html:
Goose Creek is the most populous city in Berkeley County, in the southern part of the county and inside the Charleston-North Charleston metro area. Elevation is only 13 feet. The Cooper and Back rivers mark the eastern edge, with Hanahan to the southwest and North Charleston and the unincorporated community of Ladson to the west.

The city was incorporated in 1961 and has grown in every census since, from 35,938 residents in 2010 to 45,946 in 2020, which made it the seventh largest city in the state. Most of what buyers see dates from that growth, not from the colonial past that gave the creek its name.

sections.h2: Joint Base Charleston and military sellers
sections.html:
The military is the dominant presence. Joint Base Charleston formed in 2010 when the Air Force base merged with the Naval Weapons Station. Its 628th Air Base Wing supports more than 60 Defense Department and federal agencies, and its protocol office lists 53 tenant units. The 437th Airlift Wing flies 40 C-17A aircraft and serves more than 90,000 service members, civilians, dependents and retirees.

Tenants include Naval Information Warfare Center Atlantic, Nuclear Power School, Naval Health Clinic Charleston, the South Carolina Army National Guard, the 315th and 437th Airlift Wings and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

A homeowner who gets orders can end up leaving before the house sells. Decide who will handle repairs, showings and utilities while you are away, and ask your closing attorney how to sign from out of town. A sale is still possible with a South Carolina attorney running the closing.

With 13 feet of elevation beside two rivers, insurance is a buyer's first question. Berkeley County Emergency Management says most homeowner, mobile home and rental policies leave out flood coverage, which has to be bought separately. A flood policy has a 30-day waiting period, and wind and hail coverage can carry a 15-day wait. Nobody can buy homeowner's or renter's insurance after a hurricane watch or warning is issued.

That means a buyer under contract in hurricane season may struggle to add coverage late. Make the buyer's agent's job easy:

  • Pull your current homeowner's and flood policies and have the declarations pages ready.
  • Gather roof and window replacement dates.
  • Keep records of any past water entry and what was repaired.
  • Check whether a flood policy is in force and can transfer.

Berkeley County bills real estate tax once a year, and you pay the Tax Collector in Moncks Corner. The auditor's page lays out the math: market value times the assessment ratio gives assessed value, and assessed value times the millage rate gives the tax. State law requires reassessment, usually every five years.

DateWhat happens
October 1Property tax books open
January 15Prior year's taxes due
January 16 to February 13 percent penalty
February 2 to March 16Additional 7 percent penalty

Assessment notices go out each spring, and appeals are due by a date printed on the notice. The 4 percent legal residence credit has to be applied for by January 15. State ratios are 4 percent for a qualifying primary home and 6 percent for other real property. If you rent out a Goose Creek house you used to live in, ask the county whether the 4 percent status still applies before you assume the bill will stay the same.

The City of Goose Creek takes permit applications through an online portal and enforces zoning, property maintenance and nuisance ordinances. The main line is 843-797-6220, and mail goes to 519 N. Goose Creek Boulevard, PO Drawer 1768, Goose Creek, SC 29445. The residential permit page puts these jobs through standard review:

  • Re-roofing and roof repairs
  • Water heater and HVAC equipment change-outs
  • Replacement windows and vinyl siding
  • Electrical upgrades and gas furnace change-outs
  • Minor non-structural wood rot repairs

Additions, structural repairs, landscaping, new construction and accessory structures of 200 square feet or more need review by both Planning and Zoning and the building office, which takes longer. The city also publishes a Certificate of Occupancy versus Completion guide.

If a prior owner replaced a roof or water heater, confirm the permit was closed. Code Enforcement covers property maintenance on all properties in the city, so a vacant house with overgrowth can draw a notice.

A South Carolina attorney runs the closing, and the deed is recorded with the Berkeley County Register of Deeds. Land records there go back to 1884, and the office is at PO Box 6122, Moncks Corner, phone 843-719-4084.

The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for the first $500 of value plus $1.30 for each additional $500, as the Department of Revenue page shows. The seller must deliver a written property condition disclosure before a contract is signed, unless the sale is exempt, and must correct it or make repairs if something material changes before closing.

Bring photo ID, keys, your lender's contact details and the policy papers noted above. The attorney pays off your loan and any taxes owed from the proceeds, files the deed and hands you the balance. A cash sale removes the buyer's loan approval and appraisal from that timeline.

A Goose Creek seller can list with an agent, sell without one or take a cash offer. Listing fits a house in good shape with time to spare. A cash offer fits when you are on orders, behind on payments, dealing with storm repairs or simply short on time.

Before you compare offers, do three things. Get a payoff figure from your lender. Ask the Tax Collector what, if anything, is owed. Check with the city that no permit for a roof, water heater or window job was left open. These small checks keep a buyer from lowering the price late, and they let the attorney prepare the closing papers sooner.

Remember the hurricane calendar too. A contract signed in the middle of storm season leaves less room for a buyer to line up insurance, so a short closing window helps everyone.

Public schools belong to the Berkeley County School District, 107 East Main Street in Moncks Corner, phone 843-899-8600. Goose Creek High School and Stratford High School are inside city limits, and Cane Bay High School is outside but serves students from both inside and outside. Buyers who ask about a particular school zone should get the answer from the district, since zones can change with growth.

faqs.q: Is Goose Creek in Berkeley County or Charleston County?
faqs.a: Berkeley County. Goose Creek is in the southern part of the county and is its most populous city, inside the Charleston-North Charleston metro area. Tax bills and deed recording go through Berkeley County offices.

faqs.q: When are Goose Creek property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes for a given year are payable by January 15 of the following year. A 3 percent penalty applies from January 16 to February 1, and another 7 percent from February 2 to March 16.

faqs.q: Does a flood policy take effect right away?
faqs.a: No. Berkeley County Emergency Management says flood policies have a 30-day waiting period and wind and hail coverage can have a 15-day wait. Coverage cannot be bought after a hurricane watch or warning is issued.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Goose Creek?
faqs.a: The city lists re-roofing and roof repairs among the permits that receive standard review. Apply through the online permitting portal or call 843-797-6220 to check.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Goose Creek house if I am being transferred?
faqs.a: Yes. A South Carolina attorney runs the closing, so ask that attorney how to arrange signing from out of town.
